title: Tracing a defect back to its factory

title: Two positive tests on one person
stem: A condition affects 1% of a population. A test has sensitivity 0.95 and specificity 0.90. Conditional on whether a person has the condition, repeated tests are independent.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability a person has the condition given one positive result.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the corresponding probability given two positive results, and explain why squaring the first posterior is invalid.

steps.text: The two results share the same underlying disease status. Conditional independence does not imply unconditional independence, and Bayes must update using both likelihoods.

title: A linear transformation changes the variance quadratically
stem: X takes values −1, 0, 1 and 2 with probabilities k, 2k, 3k and 4k. Let Y=3X−2.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find k, the mean of X and its variance.

title: The price of a minimum-prize guarantee
stem: A game pays X dollars, where X is 0, 4 or 10 with probabilities 0.5, 0.3 and 0.2. An optional guarantee changes the payout to Y=max(X,2).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the fair entry fee for the original game and the variance of its payout.

parts.label: b

title: Independent copies and a repeated copy
stem: X and Y are independent with the same distribution: P(0)=1/4, P(1)=1/2 and P(2)=1/4. Let U=X+Y and V=2X.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the means and variances of U and V.

steps.text: Enumerating U gives probabilities $(1,4,6,4,1)/16$ at 0,1,2,3,4, so $E(U^2)=5$.

title: The larger of two uniform measurements
stem: U and V are independent uniform random variables on [0,1]. Let M=max(U,V). The distribution function is defined by $F_M(m)=P(M\le m)$.

steps.text: M≤m requires both U≤m and V≤m.

stem: For data $(x,y)=(1,5),(2,7),(3,12),(4,13),(5,18)$, use least-squares regression of y on x.

title: A mean depends on how two groups are weighted
stem: A school has 60 students in group A with mean travel time 12 minutes and 40 in group B with mean 18 minutes. A researcher reports 15 minutes by averaging the two group means.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the correct school mean and explain the error in the report.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A proportional stratified sample of 20 is planned. State how many to select from each group and describe a random selection method that avoids convenience bias.

steps.text: A simple average of group means assigns equal weight to unequal group sizes.
Select 12 from A and 8 from B.
Number all students in each group and use a random-number generator to select the required number without replacement.
Random selection within each stratum gives every student the same sampling fraction and avoids selecting only readily available students.

title: Evidence that leaves the prior unchanged
stem: Urn A is selected with probability 1/3 and contains three red balls and one blue. Urn B is selected with probability 2/3 and contains one red and three blue. Two balls are drawn without replacement from the selected urn.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Given two red balls, find the probability A was selected.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Given exactly one red and one blue, find the posterior probability of A and explain the result.

steps.text: Two red balls are impossible from B, so the posterior probability of A is 1.
$P(\text{one of each}\mid A)=3/6=1/2$ and the same probability holds for B.
The evidence has equal likelihood under both urns, so it does not change the prior odds.
